provenance.title: store-aisle-detection.mp4
provenance.creator: Intel IoT DevKit / sample-videos contributors
provenance.changes: Original 00:08–01:00 excerpt; resampled to 15 fps; audio removed; H.264 transcoding. Analysis outputs add anonymous BBoxes, trails and dwell heatmaps.
provenance.scene: Actual housewares retail store; fixed elevated camera. Not a supermarket food aisle, simulation or generated video.
provenance.attribution: Intel IoT DevKit sample-videos contributors · CC BY 4.0 · modified excerpt

limitations: Real footage uses the person class of a pretrained MobileNet-SSD model. Occlusion, overhead views, and small people can cause missed detections.
Track IDs are temporary nearest-centroid associations. Occlusion, crossings, or re-entry can split or switch IDs; they do not identify individuals or establish an exact visitor count.
The pipeline does not infer a person's role, identity, or purchases. Zones are assigned from bounding-box centers.
Observation time is weighted by the actual intervals between frames sampled at up to 3 fps. Behavior between samples is not directly observed.
Model confidence is a detection score, not measured store-level accuracy. The heatmap accumulates observation time at detected positions.

methodology.confidence: Synthetic marker match=1; MobileNet model score is not calibrated accuracy.

render_details.attribution: Video: Intel IoT DevKit / sample-videos | CC BY 4.0 | Modified excerpt + annotations
render_details.heatmap: Measured frame sample_seconds weighted person-observation-seconds with Gaussian spatial smoothing at observed centers; normalized to the clip's maximum. Interpolation does not add heat. Not temperature.
render_details.interpolation: Adjacent tracks interpolated for display only; detections more than 0.4s away are hidden.
